hints.title: Multi-Item Bundle Selection Obstacle
hints.text: Special offers bundle quantities of items for a discounted price, but cannot exceed needed quantities. How can checking both direct item purchase and each valid special bundle recursively find the minimum spend?

hints.title: Needs State Subproblem Invariant
hints.text: The lowest cost to satisfy remaining needs tuple is the minimum over buying remaining items individually and applying any valid special offer.

hints.title: Tuple State Exploration Procedure
hints.text: Compute base cost by multiplying each item in the current needs tuple by its single-item price. For each special offer, verify that none of its item amounts exceed the current need. If valid, recursively solve for the reduced needs tuple, adding the special offer price. Cache results by needs tuple to avoid recomputation. Return the minimal cost.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of distinct items (up to 6)
B: max need per item (up to 10)
complexity.notes: At most B^N unique needs states are cached during exploration.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Uncached branching across offers takes exponential time with redundant state evaluation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: State cache stores up to B^N states to prune duplicate needs paths.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Filtering out invalid special offers that exceed current needs.
